# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My top pick is the JBL Charge 6.** It's the best all-rounder for both settings. What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and iTechGuides and BestProducts also ranked it first.
- **Water and dust rating:** IP68
- **Battery:** 20 hours, or 28 with Playtime Boost
- **Price:** about $130 at Walmart and $150 at Amazon
- **Extras:** it works as a power bank, and it has a removable carrying handle
- **Sources:** [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart), [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

## Other good options

| Need | Pick | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pool parties, loudest | JBL Boombox 4 | RTINGS' top pick. It floats, is built for long immersion, and has 40+ hours of battery. It's big and pricey, and the sound is directional. | [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| Even sound all around the pool | Ultimate Ears Epicboom | 360° sound, IP67, floats, and 15-hour battery. Tom's Guide named it best overall, and RTINGS named it best mid-range. | [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers), [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| Budget | Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 | About $65 to $67, IP67, floats, 14 hours, and a rugged rubber shell. It's small, so it won't get very loud. | [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) |
| Cheapest | JBL Go 5 | About $40, IP67, and soap-sized. Battery is only 8 hours. | [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) |
| Easy to carry | JBL Grip | About $100, IP68, under a pound, and can-shaped so it fits a bag's bottle pocket. It has 12 hours of battery. Good Housekeeping's best overall. | [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/) |

## Tips for water and sand
- **Look for IP67 or higher.** Tom's Guide and Good Housekeeping both treat this as the level to aim for at a pool or beach.
- **Rinse the speaker with fresh water after use.** IP ratings don't cover damage from salt or chlorine. Fabric-covered speakers wear fastest, according to RTINGS. Check your manual first, since some brands advise against beach use.
- **Keep it on a towel at the beach.** The Soundcore Boom 2 floats, but it has no dust rating, per BestProducts.
- **Close the charging port flap before it gets wet.** Dry the speaker fully before you plug it in.

The links above go to the review pages, which have retailer buttons for Amazon, Walmart and Best Buy. I didn't get direct product-page links in the search results. Prices are as reported in those articles and may have changed.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want something pocketable or party-loud, I can narrow this to one pick.
